svg.text: At a FIXED counting time, how flat is total precision against level? (dark 13:20 + light 13:59, f = 10 %, equal-time off run)
A. Levels within 5 % of the best total precision
B. Width of that range (5 %: solid, 10 %: dashed)
top of the scored range (18.0 mV)
How to read it. T_cross = V(best) / sigma_sys^2 is the counting time (each run) at which the counting noise at the best level equals the systematic floor from delta_f.
Counting much less than T_cross (left), the statistics dominate and the range is the photon-free 5 % band at N' = N (1 + f). Counting much longer (right), the total approaches
the systematic floor at every level, so the range spreads over most of the scored range: the threshold matters less and less, but so does the extra counting time.
The range depends only on T / T_cross and N', not on delta_f itself: a larger delta_f just makes T_cross shorter. In terms of time to reach a target precision p the range does
NOT widen (fig_total_time_vs_level): the systematic multiplies every level's time by the same factor.
eps(v) from room-light scans (light 13:59, light 17:24); b(v) from the 2026-11-10 dark scans (dark 13:20, dark 16:36), fitted by selftest._smooth_dark_rate. R8486 at ~1000 V
(operator; HV not in the files). The photon background is a MODEL: fraction f of the signal, same pulse heights, absent from the off run.
